after_molecular_targets.target_label: bacterial DNA gyrase (GyrA/GyrB) and topoisomerase IV (ParC/ParE)
after_molecular_targets.experimental_context: Purified Streptococcus pneumoniae and Escherichia coli DNA gyrase supercoiling and topoisomerase IV decatenation inhibition assays and step-wise QRDR mutant selection (Cambau et al. 2009, DOI:10.1093/jac/dkn528, PMID:19451292).

evidence.snippet: Besifloxacin is a novel chiral fluoroquinolone with potent activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative ocular pathogens through balanced inhibition of bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV.
evidence.notes: Cambau et al. 2009 (PMID:19451292) measured purified S. pneumoniae and E. coli DNA gyrase supercoiling and topoisomerase IV decatenation inhibition and step-wise QRDR mutant selection, establishing dual GyrA/GyrB and ParC/ParE target engagement.

added_history_event.changes: Added primary-literature molecular_targets entry for bacterial DNA gyrase (GyrA/GyrB) and topoisomerase IV (ParC/ParE) (PROTEIN_COMPLEX, DIRECT_BINDING_TARGET) backed by DOI:10.1093/jac/dkn528 (PMID:19451292; issue #1285).

after_molecular_targets.target_label: bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV
after_molecular_targets.experimental_context: Bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV inhibition and GyrA/ParC QRDR mutant-panel profiling with non-fluorinated quinolone T-3912 / ozenoxacin (Yamakawa et al. 2002, DOI:10.1128/AAC.46.5.1229-1234.2002, PMID:11959549).

evidence.snippet: Yamakawa et al. reported that the nonfluorinated topical quinolone T-3912 (ozenoxacin) exhibited potent antibacterial activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative pathogens, including fluoroquinolone-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pneumoniae, by inhibiting DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV.
evidence.notes: Yamakawa et al. 2002 (PMID:11959549) characterized T-3912 (ozenoxacin) activity against GyrA/ParC target-mutant staphylococcal and pneumococcal strains and established dual inhibition of bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV.

added_history_event.changes: Added primary-literature molecular_targets entry for bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV (PROTEIN_COMPLEX, DIRECT_BINDING_TARGET) backed by DOI:10.1128/AAC.46.5.1229-1234.2002 (PMID:11959549; issue #1285).

after_molecular_targets.target_label: bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV
after_molecular_targets.experimental_context: Purified bacterial DNA gyrase DNA supercoiling inhibition and topoisomerase IV decatenation assays with T-3761 / pazufloxacin (Fukuoka et al. 1993, DOI:10.1128/AAC.37.3.384, PMID:8460909; Mitsuyama et al. 2002, PMID:11959571).

evidence.snippet: Fukuoka et al. reported that T-3761 (pazufloxacin) showed potent broad-spectrum antibacterial activity against Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria and inhibited bacterial DNA gyrase supercoiling activity.
evidence.notes: Fukuoka et al. 1993 (PMID:8460909) measured direct inhibition of Escherichia coli DNA gyrase supercoiling activity by T-3761 (pazufloxacin), and Mitsuyama et al. 2002 (PMID:11959571) established dual inhibition of bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV.

added_history_event.changes: Added primary-literature molecular_targets entry for bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV (PROTEIN_COMPLEX, DIRECT_BINDING_TARGET) backed by DOI:10.1128/AAC.37.3.384 (PMID:8460909, PMID:11959571; issue #1285).

after_molecular_targets.experimental_context: Clostridioides difficile macromolecular biosynthesis and cell-free coupled transcription-translation inhibition assays demonstrating primary 50S ribosomal protein-synthesis inhibition (IC50 0.08-0.31 ug/mL) and secondary weak DNA synthesis inhibition (Locher et al. 2014, DOI:10.1093/jac/dkt411, PMID:24128668).

evidence.snippet: Cadazolid is a novel quinoxolidinone antibiotic that potently inhibits Clostridium difficile protein synthesis, including in linezolid-resistant strains, and prevents toxin A/B and spore formation while also weakly inhibiting DNA synthesis.
evidence.notes: Locher et al. 2014 (PMID:24128668) demonstrated by macromolecular labeling and cell-free translation assays in C. difficile that cadazolid acts primarily by inhibiting bacterial ribosomal protein synthesis (IC50 0.08-0.31 ug/mL), with >60-fold weaker secondary inhibition of DNA synthesis.

added_history_event.changes: Added primary-literature molecular_targets entry for bacterial 50S ribosomal subunit peptidyl-transferase center (RIBOSOMAL_SUBUNIT, DIRECT_BINDING_TARGET) backed by DOI:10.1093/jac/dkt411 (PMID:24128668; issue #1286).

after_molecular_targets.target_label: bacterial 50S ribosomal subunit peptidyl-transferase center (23S rRNA domain V)
after_molecular_targets.experimental_context: Biaryl oxazolidinone RX-1741 (radezolid) binding to the bacterial 50S ribosomal subunit 23S rRNA peptidyl-transferase center and translation inhibition in Staphylococcus aureus and linezolid-resistant strains (Locke et al. 2009, DOI:10.1128/AAC.00962-09, PMID:19752277; Skripkin et al. 2008, DOI:10.1128/AAC.01193-07, PMID:18663023).

evidence.snippet: Radezolid (RX-1741) is a novel biaryl oxazolidinone that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding to the 50S ribosomal subunit and retains potent activity against Staphylococcus aureus strains carrying 23S rRNA mutations or the cfr methyltransferase gene.
evidence.notes: Locke et al. 2009 (PMID:19752277) and Skripkin et al. 2008 (DOI:10.1128/AAC.01193-07, PMID:18663023) established that radezolid binds the bacterial 50S ribosomal subunit 23S rRNA peptidyl-transferase center with additional biaryl contacts that retain activity against cfr- and uL3/uL4-mutant ribosomes.

added_history_event.changes: Added primary-literature molecular_targets entry for bacterial 50S ribosomal subunit peptidyl-transferase center (23S rRNA domain V) (RIBOSOMAL_SUBUNIT, DIRECT_BINDING_TARGET) backed by DOI:10.1128/AAC.00962-09 (PMID:19752277; issue #1286).

after_molecular_targets.target_label: mycobacterial 50S ribosomal subunit peptidyl-transferase center (23S rRNA)
after_molecular_targets.experimental_context: Thiomorpholinyl oxazolidinone PNU-100480 (sutezolid) binding to the mycobacterial 50S ribosomal subunit 23S rRNA peptidyl-transferase center and inhibition of Mycobacterium tuberculosis protein synthesis (Williams et al. 2009, DOI:10.1128/AAC.01182-08, PMID:19075058).

evidence.snippet: Williams et al. reported that PNU-100480 (sutezolid), an oxazolidinone bacterial protein synthesis inhibitor targeting the 50S ribosomal subunit, had MICs <= 0.5 ug/mL against Mycobacterium tuberculosis and showed superior sterilizing activity to linezolid in a murine tuberculosis model.
evidence.notes: Williams et al. 2009 (PMID:19075058) characterized PNU-100480 (sutezolid) and its sulfoxide metabolite PNU-101603 as 50S ribosomal subunit translation inhibitors active against drug-susceptible and multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

added_history_event.changes: Added primary-literature molecular_targets entry for mycobacterial 50S ribosomal subunit peptidyl-transferase center (23S rRNA) (RIBOSOMAL_SUBUNIT, DIRECT_BINDING_TARGET) backed by DOI:10.1128/AAC.01182-08 (PMID:19075058; issue #1286).

after_molecular_targets.experimental_context: Acylation of essential bacterial penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) to inhibit peptidoglycan transpeptidation by the tricyclic beta-lactam (trinem) GV104326 / sanfetrinem (Singh et al. 1996, DOI:10.1128/AAC.40.9.2142, PMID:8878596).

evidence.snippet: Singh et al. reported that the tricyclic beta-lactam (trinem) sanfetrinem (GV104326) exhibited potent broad-spectrum bactericidal activity against Gram-positive, Gram-negative, and anaerobic bacteria by inhibiting bacterial penicillin-binding proteins and cell wall synthesis.
evidence.notes: Singh et al. 1996 (PMID:8878596) and Di Modugno et al. 1994 (DOI:10.1128/AAC.38.10.2362, PMID:7840571) established that GV104326 (sanfetrinem) binds essential bacterial PBPs across Gram-positive and Gram-negative pathogens and resists hydrolysis by common beta-lactamases.

added_history_event.changes: Added primary-literature molecular_targets entry for bacterial penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) (PROTEIN, DIRECT_BINDING_TARGET) backed by DOI:10.1128/AAC.40.9.2142 (PMID:8878596; issue #1286).

after_molecular_targets.target_label: bacterial penicillin-binding proteins (including MRSA PBP2a and Pseudomonas aeruginosa PBPs)
after_molecular_targets.experimental_context: High-affinity acylation of essential bacterial penicillin-binding proteins, including PBP2a (mecA) in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and PBPs in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, by CS-023 / tomopenem (Koga et al. 2005, DOI:10.1128/AAC.49.8.3239-3250.2005, PMID:16048932).

evidence.snippet: Koga et al. reported that CS-023 (R-115685, tomopenem) exhibited potent antibacterial activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa through high-affinity binding to bacterial penicillin-binding proteins, including PBP2a in MRSA.
evidence.notes: Koga et al. 2005 (PMID:16048932) and Koga et al. 2008 (PMID:18070969) demonstrated high-affinity binding of CS-023 (tomopenem) to MRSA PBP2a and P. aeruginosa PBPs, inhibiting bacterial peptidoglycan cross-linking.

added_history_event.changes: Added primary-literature molecular_targets entry for bacterial penicillin-binding proteins (including MRSA PBP2a and Pseudomonas aeruginosa PBPs) (PROTEIN, DIRECT_BINDING_TARGET) backed by DOI:10.1128/AAC.49.8.3239-3250.2005 (PMID:16048932; issue #1286).

after_molecular_targets.experimental_context: Triazole inhibition of fungal cytochrome P450 lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase (CYP51 / Erg11) blocking ergosterol biosynthesis in Candida, Cryptococcus, and Scedosporium species (Ramos et al. 1999, DOI:10.1128/AAC.43.12.2992, PMID:10582896; Carrillo and Guarro 2001, DOI:10.1128/AAC.45.7.2151-2153.2001, PMID:11408242).

evidence.snippet: UR-9825 (albaconazole) is a new triazole antifungal agent with potent broad-spectrum activity against Candida, Cryptococcus, and filamentous fungi through inhibition of fungal ergosterol biosynthesis at lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase (CYP51).
evidence.notes: Carrillo and Guarro 2001 (PMID:11408242) and Ramos et al. 1999 (DOI:10.1128/AAC.43.12.2992, PMID:10582896) established UR-9825 (albaconazole) as a potent triazole inhibitor of fungal lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase (CYP51 / Erg11).

added_history_event.changes: Added primary-literature molecular_targets entry for fungal lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase (CYP51 / Erg11) (PROTEIN, DIRECT_BINDING_TARGET) backed by DOI:10.1128/AAC.45.7.2151-2153.2001 (PMID:11408242, PMID:10582896; issue #1286).

after_molecular_targets.experimental_context: Selective 1-tetrazole coordination of fungal cytochrome P450 sterol 14-alpha-demethylase (CYP51 / Erg11) heme iron by VT-1129 / quilseconazole (Lockhart et al. 2016, DOI:10.1128/AAC.02770-15, PMID:26787697; Warrilow et al. 2016, DOI:10.1128/AAC.00349-16, PMID:27161862).

evidence.snippet: VT-1129 is a novel oral fungal-specific CYP51 inhibitor that potently inhibits Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii sterol 14-alpha-demethylase while exhibiting minimal activity against human cytochrome P450 enzymes.
evidence.notes: Lockhart et al. 2016 (PMID:26787697) and Warrilow et al. 2016 (DOI:10.1128/AAC.00349-16, PMID:27161862) demonstrated tight type II binding of VT-1129 (quilseconazole) to Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii CYP51 (Kd 11-14 nM) and potent inhibition of fungal sterol 14-alpha-demethylase activity.

added_history_event.changes: Added primary-literature molecular_targets entry for fungal lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase (CYP51 / Erg11) (PROTEIN, DIRECT_BINDING_TARGET) backed by DOI:10.1128/AAC.02770-15 (PMID:26787697, PMID:27161862; issue #1286).
